newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares surge on optimism on government steps.
newsitem.headline: India shares surge on optimism on government steps.

text.p: Indian stocks gained nearly four percent on Monday on rising hopes of the government unveiling a policy package to stimulate the capital markets and woo investment, traders said.
Indian bourses have been buoyant since the New Year in sharp contrast with the bearish mood afflicting other Asian markets and broad losses registered on Friday on Wall Street.
"There is a lot of optimism around..foreign funds are picking up stocks...they don't want to miss out on the market's upward move," said Dilip Joshi, a dealer at Prime Broking.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's top 30-share index ended Monday 127.12 points, or 3.70 percent, higher at 3,562.74, off the intra-day high of 3,578.26.
The National Stock Exchange 50-stock index rose 23.25 points, or 2.36 percent, to close at 1,009.15.
The Delhi index gained 4.9 percent to 761.53 points, the Calcutta index 14.58 points to 460.90 and the Madras index 68.40 points to 3,361.87.
The Bombay stock index has risen around 15 percent this year largely on hopes triggered by a December 31 pledge by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda to introduce market-boosting policy initiatives.
Gowda has since held confidence-boosting talks with stock exchange chiefs, industrialists and bankers on the subject.
"There's always hope and anticipation...nobody wants to get caught on the wrong side of the market," said chief dealer Sanjeev Sanghvi at James Capel B&K.
Traders said hesitation on the part of investors and local funds to sell stocks in a rising market coupled with increased speculative buy orders was stoking the price rally.
"The market looks buoyant...even smallers stocks are showing signs of taking part in the rally," said Prime's Joshi.
"People are not very lenient on the selling side...lack of liquidity of stocks is one of the major reasons spurring the market to higher levels," said Capel's Sanghvi.

The policy measures were earlier expected to be announced by mid-January. Traders now hope they will be presented before the Indian premier leaves on January 31 for a World Economic Forum meeting in Davos, Switzerland.
Some of the possible steps include allowing companies to buy back their shares to reduce an equity overhang in the market, and scrapping taxes on shareholders' dividends, analysts said.
The enthusiasm persisted despite a government dampener.

A government spokesman on Monday said Gowda, who was scheduled to address The All India Association of Industries at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT) in Bombay was not expected to announce any capital market measures.
"The visit to Bombay is not connected to the capital markets. It has nothing to do with the capital markets," he told Reuters.
Asked if a package of measures was due to be announced this week, the spokesman said: "There are always a few things on the drawing board."
Dealers said the government might also raise the ceiling on foreign institutional holdings in State Bank of India, the country's largest commercial bank, to 24 from 20 percent.
"People are realising better value..the little bit of profit-taking is nullified by fresh speculative bidding," Capel's Sanghvi said. "There is all-round buying interest in the market."
